transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-05
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Quillbyte Head of Platform), Ethan (Quillbyte SRE), Sofia (Quillbyte FinOps), Jon (Eng Mgr)

Summary:
Short orientation to Redwood Console per-route telemetry, usage analytics and cost allocation. Walkthrough focuses on how to map Quillbyte routes to cost centers, show cost breakdown by model/route, and discuss benchmarking options for batching and KV cache to drive unit economics. Customer asked about VPC/private deployment constraints, SOC 2 + KMS encryption, and how canary rollouts & fallback to smaller models affect billing.

Topics covered:
- Console per-route dashboards and how tags map to billing
- Route-level latency and token breakdowns (inbound tokens, generated tokens, caching hit rates)
- Cost allocation rules: by route, by tag, by user + allocation rollups
- Batching, KV/prefix cache, and quantization effects on per-token cost
- Dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs and burst capacity model
- Security: SSO, KMS, audit logs, data residency notes
- Pilot next steps and benchmarks

Transcript: 
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick intro — I'm Alex, AE for the West region, and Priya is our SE who will walk through the console telemetry.
[00:12] Priya (Redwood SE): Hey folks. I'll mostly drive the console, show the per-route pages, and then we'll pivot to the cost allocation piece. If anything looks weird in the transcript — sorry, the auto captions sometimes mangle names.
[00:25] Maya (Quillbyte): No worries — thanks. We're most curious about the per-route cost split and how to attribute to product teams. Also want to understand how batching + kv cache could change our monthly spend.
[00:36] Jon (Quillbyte): And timeline — we need something we can pilot inside December for a January exec review.
[00:42] Alex: Great, pragmatic. Priya, take it away?
[00:45] Priya: Cool. I'm sharing my screen — tell me if you can't see. (brief pause, typing) — can everyone see the Console home?
[00:55] Ethan (Quillbyte): Yep. UI looks familiar. That top right shows our org usage?
[00:59] Priya: Exactly. The left nav has Routes, Models, Optimize, and Billing. I'm opening Routes — this is the per-route index, each row is a route or endpoint. 
[01:12] Priya: For Quillbyte I mocked three route groups: search-suggest, doc-infer, summarizer. Each route shows 7-day tokens, avg latency p50/p95, error rate, and a cost column which is the estimated token cost plus infra adjustment.
[01:26] Sofia: That cost column — that includes our reserved capacity adjustment?
[01:29] Priya: Good question — yes, if you're on Dedicated we factor reserved credits/commitments into the unit cost; for hosted it's pure per-token with model weightings. We can toggle the costing model at the top (hosted vs dedicated).
[01:42] Maya: How do tags map? We have product-team tags in our service mesh and want to ensure they flow to the route.
[01:47] Priya: There are two ways — automatic tagging via header propagation (we detect x-team or span tags from your trace) and manual mapping in the Route Settings. You can attach multiple tags per route. The Cost Allocation page then lets you roll up by tag dimension.
[01:58] Alex: To add, the console also accepts a CSV mapping if you want to do a one-time import for historic attribution.
[02:05] Priya: Next, open an individual route — I'll open doc-infer. Top panel: volume sparkline, token composition (user tokens, assistant tokens, cache hits), and a cost-by-model pie. Note the cache-hit rate metric — that's KV/prefix caching effectiveness.
[02:21] Jon: That cache-hit metric — what's the sampling window?
[02:24] Priya: It's rolling 1h by default, we can expand to 24h or 7d. We also surface hit latency so you can differentiate cache warm vs cold.
[02:34] Ethan: If we get higher cache hits, does the console recompute estimated costs automatically?
[02:38] Priya: Yes — the cost column recalculates with the cache hit discount applied and shows both observed and projected cost if you changed cache TTL or batching profile.
[02:47] Maya: Show the projected scenario — let's say we increase cache TTL and move batching window from 5ms to 20ms.
[02:52] Priya: (click) Here: Scenario builder. You can tweak batching, cache TTL, and quantization level. It replays a day's worth of traces against model cost profiles and gives delta in monthly run-rate. Example: increasing batching to 20ms reduced per-token compute cost by ~12% in this trace, but increased latency p95 by 30ms.
[03:12] Maya: That's the tradeoff space we care about. Our product team cares less about p95 for background summarizers, more for interactive search.
[03:19] Priya: Exactly — that's why you can pin route-level SLOs and the optimizer will suggest different configs per-route.
[03:25] Ethan: How do we audit changes? If someone flips batching or TTL, how's that tracked?
[03:30] Alex: All changes are audited in the Operations log. We capture user, change diff, and a simple rollback. We can also push notifications to Slack for config changes.
[03:38] Sofia: About billing — can we export per-route cost to our chargeback system? We need daily CSVs with route -> cost center mapping.
[03:45] Priya: Yes, the Billing export supports daily granularity and includes tags, route id, model id, token counts, raw compute cost and adjusted cost lines. There's also an API to pull the same data programmatically.
[03:56] Jon: Any options for sampling / anonymizing tokens in the export? Our legal/compliance team wants zero PII in exports.
[04:02] Priya: Exports never include raw texts — only token counts and metadata. If you send traces for benchmark, we recommend tokenized, redacted traces. We also support server-side redaction hooks in Private deployments.
[04:13] Maya: Can you show a per-team rollup? I want to see how Summarizer maps to Product A vs Product B.
[04:18] Priya: Click "Allocations" — select tag = product.team. Here's a rollup widget — allocation table shows direct map and a projected cost pie with grouped tags. You can define allocation rules: strict tag, proportional by token counts, or manual adjustments.
[04:31] Sofia: Manual adjustments — can we set a percentage transfer? Sometimes infra costs are split 80/20.
[04:36] Priya: Yep, manual overrides support percentages and effective date ranges. The UI stores historical allocation so you can backfill.
[04:42] Ethan: On private deployment: we run in a VPC. Does the Console still give us the same telemetry?
[04:48] Priya: Yes — Private deployments use an agent that streams anonymized metrics to your control plane. For fully air-gapped installs we provide a local Console bundle that runs in your management plane. 
[04:58] Maya: Encryption — KMS key control for logs and audit?
[05:01] Alex: Supported. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key rotation and envelope encryption. Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM — we support syslog, Splunk, and S3 sinks.
[05:10] Jon: Ok good. On the benchmarking front — Priya, what would you run to show impact of quantization + batching for us?
[05:16] Priya: For Quillbyte we'd run three variants: baseline (no kv cache, batching 5ms, FP16), cache-enabled (TTL 30s), and aggressive batching+quant (20ms batching, int8 sim). We'll replay about 1 day of traces to estimate monthly delta and p95. We'll include token-length distributions and model switch impacts.
[05:30] Maya: Do you have expected ballpark savings numbers?
[05:33] Priya: Ballparks are model and trace dependent — but on retrieval-heavy summarizers we often see 20–40% cost reduction going from baseline to cache+batching. With quantization you can see extra 15–25% on compatible models, though sometimes quality has to be validated.
[05:48] Sofia: How do you detect quality regressions? We can't simply drop quantization without tests.
[05:52] Priya: Console integrates with Redwood Optimize evals — you can tie prompt test suites, run A/B on a sample set, and get a regression alert if output quality drops beyond threshold. We'll include that in the pilot scope.
[06:03] Ethan: About fallbacks — if a high-perf model is unavailable, do we automatically fall back to cheaper model? How is cost tracked during fallbacks?
[06:09] Priya: There's a routing policy engine — you can set fallback chains. The billing is tracked by actual model used; the Console flags fallback events so you can separate baseline cost vs fallback cost during incidents.
[06:20] Jon: Any limitations around token accounting for streaming responses? We stream partial tokens for low-latency features.
[06:26] Priya: We account for tokens as they're accepted by the runtime. Streaming doesn't lose accuracy — we also expose per-chunk latencies so you can correlate stream quality to cost.
[06:34] Maya: Great. A few clarifying questions from procurement: what compliance artifacts can you share?
[06:39] Alex: We can share SOC 2 Type II report, ISO docs, and our standard security addendum. For Private installs we can provide architecture and penetration test reports under NDA.
[06:49] Sofia: Is SSO supported for fine-grained RBAC? We need role separation for FinOps vs SRE.
[06:54] Priya: Yes SSO via SAML/OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC that maps to console features — Billing view, Deployments, Optimize.
[07:01] Maya: Cool. Can you show the demo CSV export?
[07:04] Priya: (click) Export dialog — choose date range, grouping dimension, and format. Here's an example CSV row: 2027-11-29,route:doc-infer,model:gpt-redwood-7b,team:search,requests:12,345,input_tokens:234k,output_tokens:1.1M,compute_usd:420.12,cache_savings_usd:120.05,net_cost_usd:300.07
[07:25] Jon: Nice. For our FinOps csv ingestion we'll map net_cost_usd to project codes.
[07:30] Priya: Yep — and the console can push to an S3 bucket daily so your pipeline picks it up.
[07:35] Maya: Let's talk SLA — we have a business requirement for <150ms p95 on search. How do we monitor and get alerts?
[07:42] Priya: Console has per-route SLOs with alerting hooks to PagerDuty/Slack. We also surface historical regressions and dependency latencies (model cold start, KV latency).
[07:52] Ethan: Cold starts — how does Redwood reduce cold start impact?
[07:55] Priya: We use pooled warm replicas, async prewarmed shards, and smart routing to avoid cold-starting in the happy path. You can reserve warm capacity for critical routes.
[08:05] Sofia: Any special pricing for reserved warm replicas?
[08:08] Alex: Reserved capacity has commit tiers — warm replicas factor into the reserved unit calculation. We'll put exact numbers in the pricing note.
[08:15] Maya: Can we see a short walk through of the Optimize tab?
[08:18] Priya: Sure — switching to Optimize. This surface suggests batching, cache TTL, and quantization profiles per route based on observed token lengths and SLOs. Each suggestion includes expected cost delta and risk level.
[08:30] Jon: Risk level meaning quality/regression risk?
[08:33] Priya: Yes, it's derived from historical evals and model family heuristics. We flag suggestions that need evals first.
[08:40] (brief cross-talk about network/lag)
[09:05] Ethan: One operational question — if we enable auto-optimize will it change configs automatically or just suggest?
[09:10] Priya: Both: you can enable auto-apply for non-breaking suggestions (e.g., increase cache TTL). For anything that could affect quality we default to suggestions and manual approval.
[09:20] Maya: Ok that's comforting. Anything else in telemetry we should be aware of?
[09:25] Priya: We also track per-token cost by kernel type and hardware, which helps you decide if you want to route certain routes to cheaper hardware or different regions.
[09:34] Sofia: Multi-region allocation — our billing has region tags. Can we split costs by region + team?
[09:39] Priya: Yes, allocation rules can include region dimension. You'll see a matrix in the Allocations view.
[09:45] Alex: Quick runtime note — some product names in this demo might show as 'Redwood console' in captions; apologies for that.
[09:52] Maya: (laugh) no problem.
[09:55] Priya: Switching back — close to the end I'll recap pilot scope: 1) share traces, 2) Redwood runs three benchmark configs, 3) joint eval on quality, 4) weekly sync during pilot.
[10:08] Maya: Sounds good. Sofia — any final procurement asks?
[10:11] Sofia: We need a draft MSA and a sample SOW for pilot pricing. Also, clear SLA tiers and support response times.
[10:19] Alex: We'll attach draft MSA + SOW. I'll include 30/60/90 day pilot pricing options.
[10:24] Jon: Can you also include an example of the billing CSV so our FinOps can test ingestion?
[10:28] Alex: Yep, will send a sample.
[10:31] (silence, brief typing)
[10:45] Priya: Okay that's it from the console side. Any other technical questions?
[10:48] Ethan: One more — you mentioned model switches for fallback, will that change the tokenization/counting?
[10:52] Priya: Token accounting is consistent at the runtime level. If model changes tokenization semantics, the console shows both pre- and post-token counts and flags potential delta.
[11:01] Maya: Great. If there's no more, let's move to next steps and close.
[11:05] Alex: Recap — Alex send pricing + sample CSV + MSA draft by 12/09. Priya run benchmarks and send results by 12/12. Quillbyte to share traces and tags by 12/08. Pilot kickoff week of 12/13.
[11:18] Sofia: Confirmed. We'll get the traces over to the secure S3 bucket link.
[11:22] Alex: Perfect, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and links.
[11:26] Maya: Thanks, appreciate it.
[11:28] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript imperfections: occasional speaker mislabels, product names transcribed slightly wrong ("Redwood Optimise" vs "Optimize"), and timestamps are approximate to the audio.
